title: Parallel Tool Calling in LLM Agents: When It Helps and When It Breaks
excerpt: A model that calls two tools at once isn't dangerous by itself. It's the shared state those calls both touch that breaks quietly, with no error anywhere in sight.
focus_keyword: parallel tool calling in llm agents
seo_title: Parallel Tool Calling in LLM Agents: Risks & Fixes
meta_description: Parallel tool calling in LLM agents speeds up Claude and OpenAI tool use, but shared writes can race. Real code shows the bug and the exact fix.
social_message:
A parallel tool call once double-booked the same inventory SKU. No crash. No exception.

Parallel tool calling in LLM agents compared across Claude and OpenAI: the exact race condition, real code reproducing it, and the lock + idempotency key fix that keeps the speed without the corruption.

images.title: Parallel tool calling in LLM agents: race condition on shared state
images.alt: Diagram of parallel tool calling in LLM agents: two tool calls colliding on the same database, triggering a lost update.
images.description: Shows how parallel tool calling in LLM agents can let two tool calls from the same model turn write over each other, causing a lost update with no error raised.

images.title: One model turn fanning out into independent parallel tool calls
images.alt: Diagram of one model response fanning out into three independent parallel tool calls, each hitting its own server.
images.caption: A single model turn can return several independent tool calls at once.
images.description: Illustrates how one assistant turn in parallel tool calling can contain multiple independent tool_use or tool_calls entries, each targeting its own tool.

images.title: Read-modify-write race condition in parallel tool calls
images.alt: Diagram of two parallel tool calls reading the same stock value before writing back, causing a lost update.
images.caption: Two parallel tool calls reading the same value before either writes back.
images.description: Depicts the read-modify-write race condition from parallel tool calling in LLM agents: both calls read the same starting value, so one write overwrites the other.

images.title: Handling a failed dependent tool call with a retry loop
images.alt: Diagram of a failed first tool call marking a dependent second call as not executed, looping back to the model for a retry.
images.caption: A failed call in a dependent batch should be marked, not silently dropped.
images.description: Shows the documented pattern for a dependent tool call batch: mark the skipped call as not executed and let the model reissue it on the next turn.
